battle.name: 周槃之戰
battle.brief: 開皇二年（582）冬，隋文帝楊堅乘陳宣帝新崩之際下詔大舉伐陳，隋軍分道出師，戰線很快壓到淮南的周槃一帶，與陳朝守軍在湖沼水網之間互相試探。這一役裡真正的短兵器並不是羅馬短劍，但它所代表的位置很清楚：盾後那一刺的節奏，正是隋陳步卒貼盾肉搏時賴以取勝的東西。

kit.name: 羅馬短劍
kit.history: 刺劍不是用來揮砍的。短兵相接靠的是盾的邊緣和刺突的節奏。

countries: 開皇二年（582）冬，隋文帝楊堅以晉王楊廣為行軍元帥、高頍為元帥長史，調集諸道兵馬大舉伐陳，是隋陳七年戰爭的開端。隋軍分道出師：一路自河南、潁川一帶東出，一路由賀若弼、韓擒虎等將領自廣陵、廬江一線南下，王世充等部則自襄陽趨荊襄，兵力和調度都歸元帥幕府支配。隋軍的編制以軍為單位，將領多有北周、西魏舊部，兵源除關隴府兵與鄉兵外，還有河南、淮南降眾以及州郡徵發的丁壯，攻城與水戰兵力另設專門將校；陳方則倚江南世族與州郡部曲，以陳宣帝陳頊新喪、朝政初轉的陳朝應戰，陳後主陳叔寶坐鎮建康，以郢州、壽春、歷陽、洞口一線的守軍構成江淮防禦，宿將吳明徹、蕭摩訶等人分領兵權。兩軍在江淮水網地帶相持，周槃一役正是這條戰線上的一場遭遇戰，只是文獻對該役雙方指揮體系的細節記載有限。
countriesEn: In the winter of 582, Emperor Wen of Sui, Yang Jian, took his second son Yang Guang as supreme commander and Gao Jiong as chief of staff, mustering armies from several circuits for a full-scale campaign against the Chen dynasty, the opening move of the seven-year Sui–Chen war. The Sui forces marched out along several axes: one thrust eastward from Henan and the Ying river region, one led by He Ruobi and Han Qinhu down the line of Guangling and Lujiang, while a force under Wang Shichong moved out from Xiangyang toward the Jing and Xiang regions. Troops and movements alike were all handled through the headquarters of the supreme commander. The Sui army was organised in army units, and many of its commanders were veterans of Northern Zhou and Western Wei; besides the Guanzhong–Longyou household troops and local levies, its strength also came from surrendered men of Henan and Huainan together with the young men levied from the prefectures and counties, while engineers and river troops were placed under separate specialist commands. The Chen, for their part, relied on the great southern families and on the local district levies, and answered with a court still adjusting to the death of Emperor Xuan of Chen, Chen Xu, the new Emperor Hou of Chen, Chen Shubao, sitting in Jiankang, with the garrisons of Yingzhou, Shouchun, Liyang and Dongkou forming the river defence and veterans such as Wu Mingche and Xiao Moha holding separate commands. The two armies stalemated in the watery country of the middle Yangtze, and the fighting at Zhoupan was an engagement on that line, though the literature preserves little detail about the command structure on either side in it.
people: 周槃一役的直接指揮者，傳世文獻並無完整記載，只能從隋陳七年戰爭的整體部署推知其輪廓。隋文帝楊堅是決策者，開皇二年十月下詔大舉伐陳，指定次子楊廣為行軍元帥；高頍任元帥長史，統籌全軍分道與糧秣，籌劃周密，是這場戰爭真正的主謀。隋文帝發兵前先問計，高頍力主分道進擊，避免一處受阻而全局停滯，隋軍的戰線因此得以同時壓向淮南與江東。賀若弼、韓擒虎分統精銳，韓擒虎尤其善於率精騎夜襲，兩人是淮南與江東方向的前鋒。陳方，宣帝陳頊於開皇二年年初病逝，皇位交接之際人心浮動，換防拖延令江淮各堡守軍銜接不順；陳後主陳叔寶以新君之身坐鎮建康，宿將吳明徹、蕭摩訶等分守要地。據《隋書》《資治通鑑》所載各役將領名位，可以確定周槃方向必有隋、陳雙方主將率部入戰，但具體人名、交戰次序與生死，諸史均未詳記，姑存其闕。
peopleEn: Those who actually commanded at Zhoupan are not preserved as such in the transmitted records; their outline can only be reconstructed from the overall deployment of the Sui–Chen war. Emperor Wen of Sui, Yang Jian, was the decision maker: in the tenth month of Kaihuang 2 (582) he issued the edict for a general attack on Chen and appointed his second son Yang Guang as supreme commander. Gao Jiong, as chief of staff, planned the deployment of the whole army along the several axes and directed its supplies, and it was he who was the real architect of the campaign. Yang Jian consulted him before the troops were sent out, and Gao insisted on striking along several separate routes so that a check in one place would not stall the whole war; the Sui line was therefore able to press towards Huainan and Jiangdong at the same time. He Ruobi and Han Qinhu each commanded picked forces, and Han Qinhu in particular was known for leading night raids with a small body of cavalry; the two were the spearhead on the Huainan and Jiangdong approaches. On the Chen side, Emperor Xuan, Chen Xu, had died at the beginning of Kaihuang 2, and the change of emperor left the court unsettled, while delays in rotating the garrisons left the outposts along the middle Yangtze badly joined up to one another. The new Emperor Hou, Chen Shubao, sat in Jiankang, and veterans such as Wu Mingche and Xiao Moha were posted to the key points of the line. The lists of officers preserved in the History of Sui and the Comprehensive Mirror for the various engagements of the war show that commanders on both sides certainly led troops into the fighting at Zhoupan, but neither the names, nor the order of the clash, nor the fate of the men are recorded; the point is left open here.
kits: 這張卡的兵器是羅馬短劍（gladius），它並不會出現在公元五八二年的長江以北戰場上；它在周槃之戰的體系裡佔據的是「刺擊型短劍」這個位置。所謂短劍，羅馬人自公元前一百年前後便大量配發給列兵，長約六十公分，雙刃而重心靠前，用途是貼盾突刺而非揮砍。陳隋的近戰兵器體系與之不同：步兵普遍裝備環首直刀與長矛，騎兵用槊，重裝單位另有大盾與長槊；唐刀式的直刃佩刀要到隋唐才定型。兩者真正相同之處，在於短兵相接的節奏：盾牌的邊緣頂住對方的槍鋒，盾後的士兵再以短刃刺出，這就是短劍原型所代表的用途。隋軍重裝單位在開皇初年已開始裝備明光形制的札甲與兜鍪，馬鎧仍以皮札為主；攻城裝備包括巢車、雲梯、擲石機與床弩，陳軍則倚城堞、弩臺與水障。當時尚無火藥兵器，勝負全在冷兵器、體力與糧秣之間。
kitsEn: The weapon on this card is the Roman gladius, and it did not appear on any battlefield north of the Yangtze in the year 582; in the order of battle at Zhoupan it occupies the place of the thrusting short sword. The Romans had issued short swords in bulk to rank and file from around 100 BC: about sixty centimetres long, double-edged, with the balance of the blade toward the point, and intended for a stab from behind the shield rather than a swung blow. The close-combat weapons of the Chen and Sui armies worked differently: infantry carried ring-pommel straight sabres and long spears, cavalry carried lances, and armoured units had large shields and lances as well, while the straight single-edged sabre of the Tang type was only taking shape in the Sui and Tang. What the two systems really share is the rhythm of hand-to-hand fighting: the edge of the shield locks the enemy's spearhead, and the man behind the shield answers with a thrust of a short blade, and that is the role the short-sword archetype plays here. Sui armoured units were already using plate-and-leather armour of the Mingguang type and iron helmets in the early Kaihuang years, while horse armour was still mostly boiled leather; the siege train included gangplank towers, scaling ladders, stone-throwers and crossbows on frames, and the Chen relied on ramparts, bolt towers and water barriers. There was no gunpowder weapon of any kind at this date, so every decision was settled between cold steel, physical endurance and grain.
tactics: 南北朝江淮作戰的通則，是先以弩手與長槊兵結陣，把騎兵留在陣後待命。周槃一役所在的是淮水與巢湖、合肥一帶交錯的湖沼水網，隋軍自北而南推進，必須沿著有限的可通行陸路與淺灘行軍，隊形一旦被水系切斷就難以展開。隋軍的戰法是先以輕騎前出試探，逼迫陳軍離開城池與堰壘，再以步卒壓上，用盾陣吸收陳軍的弩矢與撞擊，最後由突騎插入缺口；陳軍則以城池、津渡與水寨為依託，閉門不出，待隋軍立足未穩或夜間渡水之際再以精騎反擊。雙方亦常用夜襲與火攻，隋軍曾以小股精騎夜襲沿江津渡，陳軍則在堰壘、柴木與拒馬之後布置弩手，等待對方腳步未齊再以弩箭齊射。補給線是這一戰區最吃緊的一環：隋軍自河南運糧到淮南，靠的是潁、淮、泗諸水與沿途倉場，冬季水淺結冰會使運糧減慢，遠征深入的部隊往往因糧秣斷續而被迫回撤。
tacticsEn: The general rule of warfare on the middle Yangtze in the Northern and Southern dynasties was to form up crossbowmen and long-spear infantry first, and to keep the cavalry in reserve behind the line. Zhoupan lay in a country of interlocking lakes and marshes around the Huai, the Chaohu and Hefei, and the Sui army advancing from north to south had to march along a few usable roads and shallows; once the water system cut the column, it could not be deployed. Sui practice was to send light cavalry out first to probe, force the Chen to leave their cities and dikes, then bring up infantry to press them, absorb the bolts and the weight of the Chen charge behind a wall of shields, and finally send lancers into the gap. The Chen held on to their cities, fords and river stockades, kept the gates shut, and waited for the Sui to settle insecurely or to ford at night before counter-attacking with their best cavalry. Both sides also relied on night attacks and fire; the Sui sent small bodies of picked cavalry to raid the fords along the river by night, while the Chen massed crossbowmen behind dikes, brushwood and cheval-de-frise, waiting until the enemy's footfalls were out of step before loosing a volley. Supply was the tightest part of this theatre: grain moved from Henan to Huainan by the rivers Ying, Huai and Si and by the depots along the way, and in winter, when the water ran shallow and froze, transport slowed, so columns that pressed too far forward were often forced to withdraw when the grain stopped coming.
data: 關於周槃一役，能夠落實的數字有限。《隋書·高祖紀》記開皇二年十月「詔大舉伐陳」，是這場戰爭可靠的時間坐標；同一記載體系下，隋朝在全面伐陳年份留下的規模數字可供對照：開皇五年（585）楊堅下令造五牙大艦，每艦可容戰士約百二十人，分層設樓，成為後來渡江的骨幹；開皇九年（589）終於滅陳時，隋軍出動八十四軍、五十一萬八千甲士，並運糧六十萬石。相較之下，開皇二年冬的首度出兵，文獻只以「大舉」「眾軍」帶過，未留下確切的兵員與損耗數字。周槃這樣的地方小戰，兩軍投入的兵馬通常以數千至數萬計，傷亡更無從核實。距離與日期亦然：周槃的具體里位至今沒有定論，因此這裡只把可以查證的年份、月份與軍隊規模列出，不作臆測的推算；把它記在十月，取的是詔令大舉伐陳的時點。
dataEn: Few concrete figures survive for the fighting at Zhoupan. The History of Sui, in the annals of Emperor Gaozu, records for the tenth month of Kaihuang 2 (582) the edict for a general attack on Chen, and that is the one reliable date for this campaign; the scale figures the Sui left for the years of the full offensive can serve as a comparison. In Kaihuang 5 (585) Yang Jian ordered the building of five-toothed great warships, each able to carry about one hundred and twenty men on several decks, which became the backbone of the later crossing; when the Chen were finally destroyed in Kaihuang 9 (589), the Sui fielded eighty-four armies and 518,000 armed men and moved 600,000 bushels of grain. By contrast, the first offensive of the winter of Kaihuang 2 is described in the literature only as 'a general attack' and 'the massed armies', and leaves no exact figures for numbers or losses. An engagement on a place like Zhoupan would typically have involved some thousands to tens of thousands of men, and the casualties cannot be verified at all. Distances and dates are in the same condition: the exact site of Zhoupan has never been settled, so only the years, months and army scales that can be checked are given here, with no speculative arithmetic; its placement in the tenth month follows the date of the edict for the general attack.
cause: 打起上來的直接原因，是隋朝要解決一個結構性問題：北方的兵力和糧食集中在關中與河南，而陳朝控制的江南是當時最富庶的產糧區，卻尚未被北方政權整合。開皇二年之前，隋的策略是「先令南方自敗」——陳朝內部連年宮廷變動、宗室與權臣互相傾軋，陳宣帝晚年削弱陳氏宗室而倚重外姓，皇位交接時人心浮動，隋主楊堅判斷此時用兵代價最小，於是下詔大舉伐陳。就周槃一役而言，它屬於這次全面進攻的前哨戰：隋軍要把戰線推到淮水、巢湖一帶，奪取陳軍在淮南的據點與渡口，為下一步沿江推進做準備。此外，隋朝在關中與河南屯糧積兵多年，開皇初年又疏浚渠道、修整驛道，前線補給可以支撐遠出；陳朝則因連年用兵於長江中游與北朝對峙，府庫空虛，難以支持一場持久戰。
causeEn: The immediate reason for the fighting was a structural problem: the troops and the grain of the north were concentrated in Guanzhong and Henan, while the richest grain-growing region in the empire, Jiangnan, was held by the Chen and had not yet been integrated by a northern regime. Before Kaihuang 2 the Sui strategy was to let the south defeat itself: the Chen court had seen years of palace upheaval and factional struggle between the imperial clan and the powerful ministers, and in his last years Emperor Xuan had weakened the Chen princes while leaning on men from outside the family; with the throne changing hands the mood of the state was unsettled, and Yang Jian judged that this was the moment when the cost of war would be lowest, so he issued the edict for a general attack. As far as Zhoupan is concerned, the engagement belonged to the forward part of that offensive: the Sui meant to push the line to the Huai and the Chaohu, take the Chen depots and fords in Huainan, and prepare the way for the next step down the river. In addition, the Sui had stored grain and stationed troops in Guanzhong and Henan for years, and in the early Kaihuang years they dredged channels and repaired the post roads, so that the forward lines could be supplied for operations at a distance; the Chen, by contrast, had fought along the middle Yangtze against the northern courts for years on end, their treasuries were empty, and they could hardly sustain a long war.
impact: 周槃這樣的遭遇戰本身沒有改變任何王朝的版圖，但它屬於隋陳七年戰爭的開端，長遠影響卻不小。開皇二年的出兵雖然沒有渡江，卻讓陳朝看清了北方的新式戰力：隋軍有規模化的騎兵、集中的弩兵群與可以快速推進的後勤體系，陳軍沿用的舊式城防與州郡徵發已難以抵擋。更實際的是，此役之後隋朝改變策略，不再急於強渡，而是花了七年時間造大艦、修河道、儲糧於江淮；開皇五年造五牙大艦，並在山東、江南一帶儲糧修渠，都是這次挫敗的直接回應。到開皇九年，隋軍八十四軍、五十一萬八千甲士壓境，陳朝在江防崩潰後迅速崩解，第二年便被北周取代，周旋了三十餘年的南朝最後一個王朝就此結束。對後世而言，這一役也是隋唐軍制的起點之一：隋在淮南與江淮留下的據點、倉場與河渠，後來成為唐初經營江南的基礎；陳亡之後，長江流域重新統一，隨之而來的是大批北人南遷與江南士族在隋唐政治中的重新洗牌。
impactEn: An engagement like Zhoupan changed no map by itself, but it belonged to the opening of the seven-year Sui–Chen war and its long-term effect was not small. The expedition of Kaihuang 2 did not cross the river, yet it let the Chen see clearly what the new northern power had become: standardised cavalry, massed crossbowmen and a logistics system able to move forward quickly; the old-style city defences and the county levies the Chen still relied on could no longer hold. More practically, after this campaign the Sui changed its method. Instead of hurrying to force a crossing, it spent seven years building great warships, repairing canals and storing grain along the middle Yangtze; the five-toothed great ships of Kaihuang 5 and the depots and channels dug in the Jiangdong and Huainan regions were direct answers to the failure of 582. When in Kaihuang 9 the Sui came down with eighty-four armies and 518,000 armed men, the Chen defence collapsed quickly, and the last dynasty of the Southern Courts, which had lasted barely more than thirty years, was extinguished. For later ages the engagement was also one of the starting points of the Sui–Tang military system: the depots, storehouses and channels the Sui left along the Huai and the middle Yangtze became the foundation of the Tang settlement in Jiangnan; and with the fall of Chen the Yangtze valley was reunited, which brought large numbers of northerners south and reshuffled the position of the southern great families in Sui and Tang politics.
result: 就周槃一役本身而言，可以確定的結果是：隋軍在江淮前線取得了戰術上的主動，陳軍退守既有的城池、堰壘與水寨，沒有被全殲，但隋軍也未能藉此突破江防、渡過大江。開皇二年冬的整體結果是全線退兵，隋朝沒有拿下淮南的關鍵津渡，第一次伐陳以失敗告終；此後隋朝花費七年重新準備，直至開皇九年才真正完成滅陳。雙方在這一役都沒有決定性的損失，陳朝因此得以延續七年，隋朝則贏得了更寶貴的經驗：以冷兵器軍隊強渡長江，最大的難題不是岸上的陳軍，而是水上的船與後方的糧。從器物角度看，這一役也留下可以印證的細節：南北朝的近戰傷亡主要來自刺、割與撞擊而非砍劈，短兵器在貼盾時的用法，與羅馬短劍的刺擊邏輯相通，只是中原的環首刀更偏向劈砍，這也是這件兵器被放在這張卡上的原因。因此周槃之戰在戰史上的位置，更像一場試探與試錯：它測出了江淮防線的厚度，也測出了北方新王朝的耐性。
resultEn: For the engagement at Zhoupan itself the result that can be stated with confidence is this: the Sui gained the tactical initiative on the middle Yangtze front, the Chen withdrew behind their existing cities, dikes and river stockades and was not wiped out, but the Sui also failed to break through the river defence and cross the great river. The outcome of the whole winter campaign of Kaihuang 2 was a general withdrawal; the Sui took none of the key fords of Huainan, and the first attempt on the Chen ended in failure. After that the Sui spent seven years preparing again and did not complete the destruction of the Chen until Kaihuang 9. Neither side suffered decisive losses here: the Chen dynasty was granted seven more years of life, and the Sui gained something more valuable, namely experience, for in a cold-weapon war the hardest problem in carrying an army across the Yangtze was not the Chen troops on the bank but the boats on the water and the grain behind them. From the point of view of equipment the engagement also leaves a detail that can be checked: in the Northern and Southern dynasties the wounds of hand-to-hand fighting came mainly from stabbing, cutting and crushing rather than from chopping, the short blade was used from behind the shield, and that use corresponds to the thrusting logic of the Roman gladius, except that the Chinese ring-pommel sabre leaned more towards the cut, which is why this weapon is the one placed on this card. The place of the battle of Zhoupan in military history is therefore that of a probe and a test: it measured the thickness of the middle Yangtze defence, and it measured the patience of the new northern dynasty.
